Melnytsya Podilska Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ternopilska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This record shows a tension worth noting: it is categorized as 'fenced and protected,' yet the source's demolished field marks it as 'yes.' Melnytsya-Podilska's Jewish community, which became independent in the 1840s, produced the rabbi Meshulam Roth, author of the religious text Kol Mevasser, in the late 19th century. In the early 20th century, a small Hasidic court was established here by Shalom Yosef Friedman (1871–1927), grandson of the firstborn son of Israel of Ruzhin — another branch of the same Ruzhin Hasidic dynasty documented at several other sites in this collection. Jews who fled the 1942 deportations were found and murdered at this cemetery. This is the older of Melnytsya-Podilska's two Jewish cemeteries, existing by 1795 according to epigraphic data, and used until the new cemetery opened in the early 1900s.
